In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the onset does affect the weight of the syllable.
the weight of the syllable is determined in the first instance by the rime, but that onset properties may also be taken into account.
onset weight effects exist and are significant in some cases, and that onset weight effects are a universal property of syllable weight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the onset is not a mere appendix to the syllable, but rather a crucial component in the syllabic structure of the word.
we show that the onset is a significant attracter of stress, both in nonce words and in the lexicon, and that this effect is highly systematic, and unlikely to be driven by the analogy.
we are interested in the phonetics and phonology of the onset.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the domain of stress is the syllable, and that the rime is a subdomain of the syllable.
syllable weight is a gradient, perceptual property of syllables, which is sensitive to the properties of both the rime and the onset.
the syllable is not a monolithic domain for weight, but a complex system in which the rime and onset are differentially weighted.
